source_text: Nequaquam te acquiescere eruditorum sententiis, ut addas, secundum quod intellectui tuo congruit dixisse Apostolum, quia stultam fecit Deus sapientiam mundi [n39] ; disputatores vero nostros sine metu a te posse despici, quod nulla auctoritate talium premaris.
pass_a_gloss: that you by no means acquiesce to the sentences of the learned, so that you add, according to what fits your understanding, that the Apostle said that God made foolish the wisdom of the world; but that our disputers can be despised by you without fear, because you are pressed by no authority of such men.
pass_b_english: that you will never accept the judgments of the learned. You will add that the apostle said, in the sense your understanding gives it, that “God has made the wisdom of the world foolish” (1 Corinthians 1:20). You can therefore safely despise our debaters, you will say, because no authority of theirs weighs upon you.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
